title: serving: gated fast-path + precision-toggle for KV-cache continuous batching with safe-mode fallback
author: Anjali Rao
release_notes: Add gated fast-path for KV-cache + precision toggle with a safe-mode fallback. Improves tail latency for common streaming workloads; safe-mode preserves deterministic correctness for sensitive workloads.
description: Motivation: Continuous batching + KV-cache fast paths reduce per-token latency but occasionally diverge in numeric results when aggressive low-precision kernels are used or when scheduling-based micro-batching reorders work. This PR introduces a gated fast-path and a runtime precision toggle plus a safe-mode that forces conservative, fully-validated code paths to guarantee bit-for-bit reproducibility for customers who require it. Summary of changes: 1) Fast-path gating: add runtime heuristics and config flags that enable the fast kernel only when sequence-length distribution, model-arch, and hardware kernel profile match the validated fast-path profile. 2) Precision toggle: allow per-model/per-route override between fp16/fp32/quantized evaluation modes; the serving runtime will choose compatible kernels and may fallback to safe-paths when precision mismatch risks correctness. 3) Safe-mode: global and per-route safe-mode that disables precision toggles and forces validated kernels and additional validation checks (KV CRC checks, optional deterministic KV-cache replay) before emitting outputs. 4) Scheduler integration: the request router now annotates batches with fast-path eligibility metadata; the batching layer avoids merging incompatible requests that would otherwise force slow-path execution. 5) Tests, docs, and benchmarks: unit tests for gating logic, new e2e perf harness showing tail-latency improvements, and a docs page describing tradeoffs and recommended configs. Backwards-compatible: defaults preserve existing behavior (fast-path off unless model is in the validated list). See linked Linear tasks ENG-4124 (fast-path rollout) and ENG-4191 (safe-mode for enterprise).

review_conversation: Marco Silva (reviewer): Looks good overall. A few questions about the default gating thresholds — do we have telemetry to tune these safely?

Author (Anjali Rao): We collected kernel profiles from top 20% of production traffic (see bench artifacts). Defaults are conservative; flags can be toggled per-customer. Added a note in docs about telemetry and recommended rollout steps.
Yvonne Chen (reviewer): Safe-mode is important for customers with strict determinism. Can we ensure safe-mode also disables kernel autotuner?
Author: Good catch — added a guard in the kernel_registry to bypass autotuner when serving.safe_mode=true. Added unit test.
Ravi Patel (reviewer): We saw a flaky kv-cache CRC test in CI — was that root-caused?
Author: That was a race in test harness cleanup. Fixed by serializing the test fixture teardown; added a comment. CI re-run passed.
Marco Silva: Approving after nit fixes.
perf_summary: Bench (continuous-batching, 8x A100 equivalent): median per-token latency unchanged, 95th-tail latency reduced by ~18% for gated fast-path workloads; throughput improved 6% under mixed precision enabled. Safe-mode incurs 10-12% higher latency versus fast-path but matches pre-fastpath numeric outputs.
notes_for_ops: Ops: to enable broad fast-path rollout set serving.fast_path.enabled=true and add models to serving.fast_path.validated_models. For deterministic/regulatory workloads, set serving.safe_mode=true (force fp32 and validated kernels). Monitor 'fastpath.eligibility_denied' metric during rollout.
